name: Dumbbell Reverse Lunge
summary: A lunge where you step backward, which is often easier on the knees and balance than a forward lunge and loads the glutes and quads.
setup: Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Stand tall with your feet about hip width apart.
Brace your trunk and set your shoulders back.
execution: Step one foot straight back and land on the ball of your foot.
Lower your hips until your front thigh is about parallel and your back knee nearly touches the floor.
Keep most of your weight on the front foot with the torso upright.
Push through the front foot to return to standing, bringing your back foot back to the start.
Repeat on the same leg or alternate legs.
mistakes: Front knee collapsing inward: push it out in line with the toes.
Taking too short a step so the front knee shoots far forward: step back farther.
Pushing off the back foot: drive through the front foot to stand.
Leaning forward: keep your chest up and brace your trunk.
